reason: E1 shows in situ neutron diffraction tracks lattice strains and yields diffraction elastic constants in a similar alloy, supporting the first two premises. E2 shows XRD peak broadening can quantify local lattice strains in multi-component systems, supporting the third premise. However, neither E1 nor E2 addresses microbeam deconvolution of overlapping signals or a direct correlation between lattice strain gradients and global yield/fracture behavior, leaving the last two premises unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: In situ XRD/ND can track lattice strain evolution during elastic deformation of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Diffraction elastic constants derived from lattice strain vs. applied stress can be used to assess elastic isotropy/anisotropy.
Peak broadening in XRD can quantify local lattice strains and structural inhomogeneity in multi-component alloys.
Microbeam diffraction mapping can deconvolute overlapping signals from different heterostructural domains.
Lattice strain gradients at interfaces directly correlate with global yield and fracture behavior.
